name: JUNO — Yangjiang and Taishan reactor complexes at the 52-53 km baseline
notes: Core numbering YJ-1..6 / TS-1..2 is assigned by matching the order of the measured distances to the order of the published baselines; the OSM ways carry no unit numbers. The Taishan EPR units 3 and 4 (baselines 52.32 and 52.20 km in the CDR) were not built; arXiv:2104.02565 says only that two more cores 'possibly' may be built.
Far reactors: arXiv:2104.02565 Sec. 1.2 puts the Daya Bay complex 215 km (and Huizhou 265 km) from the detector, beyond a local map; Daya Bay has its own map (linked).

Residual: the Yangjiang buildings are 84-125 m farther from the published hall coordinate than the surveyed baselines say, the Taishan buildings agree to <= 16 m. The sign pattern is that of a ~100 m displacement of the published coordinate toward SSW, or of an OSM registration offset between the two plants; the sources cannot separate them.

summary.plain: The detector and the two nuclear power plants whose antineutrinos it measures, to scale: Yangjiang (six reactors) and Taishan (two reactors in operation), each about 52-53 km from the JUNO hall.
summary.technical: Baseline map: published hall coordinate (arXiv:2104.02565), OSM reactor buildings of Yangjiang (six building=reactor ways) and Taishan (two nuclear-island buildings), with each building's centroid-to-hall distance checked against the GPS-surveyed baselines of Table 1 at 0.3 % tolerance. Companion to map:juno-jiangmen.
